title: Stonehaven Systems — GPU onramp & VPC integration exploratory call
header: Date: 2026-03-29 | Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~42m | Recording: auto | Location: Zoom
summary: Introductory partner discovery. Stonehaven is evaluating GPU onramp and channel integration options for their SaaS ML pipeline; key constraints are data residency in EU, KMS integration, and hybrid on-prem latency profiles. Redwood AE + SE walked through deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private), routing/fallback, and cost/latency tradeoffs. Customer requested pilot sizing guidance, security docs (SOC2, ISO), and a small benchmark plan for 2 models across hosted and private deployment - agreed to share next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the cloud partners program. We've got Carlos and Hannah with me. How's it going?
[00:08] Lena (VP Eng): Hi, thanks. Busy day, appreciate you squeezing this in.
[00:11] Omar: Yeah thanks. Omar here, head of cloud partnerships at Stonehaven.
[00:15] Priya (Security): Priya - security lead, I'll mainly focus on compliance q's.
[00:18] Carlos (SE): Quick intro — I'm Carlos, I work on infra integrations and performance; I'll run through latency/cost tradeoffs and pilot ideas.
[00:25] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: 1) hear about your current stack and goals, 2) run through how Redwood would fit (hosted, dedicated, private), 3) talk pilot/benchmarks and security. Sound good?
[00:34] Daniel (Infra): Yep. For context — Stonehaven runs a multi-tenant SaaS for log analytics, heavy embedding + rerank workloads. Primary region EU-West, we keep customer PII in EU datastores. We use GCP and some on-prem colocation for latency-sensitive customers.
[00:48] Maya: Thanks, that's useful. What's CPU/GPU currently?
[00:51] Daniel: Mostly CPU for feature extraction, but we've been spinning up A100s for a few customers. We're hitting cost/ops limits — want a partner to offload inference and handle predictable throughput.
[01:03] Omar: We're also evaluating partnerships to provide a hybrid onramp offering to our channel partners — they want consistent SLAs.
[01:09] Carlos: Makes sense. Two axes we usually see: cost/latency and control/isolation. Hosted is fastest to onboard, Dedicated gives reserved pools, Private gives full control (VPC / on-prem).
[01:20] Priya: For us security is key — we need SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, audit logs, customer-managed keys (KMS or HSM), and data residency controls. Can Redwood support those in private mode?
[01:33] Hannah (SE): Yes, private deployments support a customer-managed control plane, KMS integrations, and VPC peering. We also offer audit log forwarding and can run in an EU-only region or on-prem package for air-gapped customers. We'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs after.
[01:46] Priya: Great. Are there any gotchas with cert rotation or KMS lifetime?
[01:50] Carlos: We support several KMS providers; rotation can be automated. For private on-prem, you'll manage keys but we provide the hooks for automatic rotation. We'll share the diagrams.
[01:58] Lena: From product side — we need sub-100ms for short chat reranking at 64 tokens, and embeddings throughput for batch jobs. What does Redwood hit on that?
[02:08] Carlos: Short answer — depends on model and batching. For 64 tokens with an optimized Llama-ish model on a p4-equivalent, 60-120ms p99 is typical in our benchmarks. With caching and continuous batching you can get latency lower for repeated prefixes. For embeddings batch jobs, we recommend dedicated capacity with autoscale to smooth cost.
[02:28] Daniel: Any variance when moving to private deployment?
[02:31] Carlos: Minimal if you use same GPU class/driver stack. The runtime chooses kernels and quantization paths; sometimes private installs lag a bit on kernel updates but we provide stable builds.
[02:41] Omar: Partner integration question — we want to resell a white-labeled onramp. What model of partnership works? Channel reseller? Embedded offering?
[02:49] Maya: We do several models — reseller, co-managed dedicated pools, and OEM private bundles. We can map to your channel economics. We have partners who run dedicated pools for resellers with routing policies.
[02:59] Priya: Practical question — can Redwood attest to model provenance and licensing for open weights? We need compliance for certain customers.
[03:06] Hannah: We keep a model catalog with provenance metadata; we can commit to model licensing checks and provide version manifests in the control plane.
[03:13] Lena: Great. About pilot/benchmarks — we want two models: an embedding model and a convo model. Test across hosted and private (EU on-prem) with our 3 workload patterns. How do we size the pilot?
[03:24] Carlos: Typical pilot: 2-4 weeks, run identical workloads through hosted Redwood and then a private deployment with same GPU class. We'll measure latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, and ops effort. For GPU sizing, we suggest starting with 1-2 GPUs (A100 or H100 equiv) for dev + 4 GPUs for scaled throughput tests — but we can produce a tailored sizing matrix after we see QPS and token lengths.
[03:47] Daniel: We can share anonymized query histograms.
[03:50] Maya: Yes please, send histograms and peak QPS. We'll run a quick throughput calc and propose a pilot BOM.
[03:56] Omar: Licensing/contract questions — what kind of MSA do we need for channel programs?
[04:01] Maya: We have a partner MSA template and reseller addendum. We'll share redacted versions.
[04:07] Priya: On observability — do you provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-model dashboards we can forward to customers?
[04:12] Hannah: Yes — Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token costs, tracing hooks for inference calls and KV cache hit rates. You can send dashboards as embeds to clients.
[04:21] Lena: Any known performance regressions with quantized weights? We use int8 quant in some pipelines.
[04:25] Carlos: Quantization tradeoffs vary by model. We have quantization profiles and quality monitors in Redwood Optimize. We can recommend quantization for batch embeddings to cut cost, and run evals to measure regressions.
[04:36] Maya: Quick note — some transcriptions make our product names odd; we call out Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private — sometimes the transcript spellings are off, sorry.
[04:43] (laughter)
[04:45] Omar: No worries.
[04:46] Maya: Any blockers on your side for an initial pilot?
[04:48] Lena: We need signoff from procurement for pilot budget and Priya needs to review the security docs; also we need more clarity on SSO integration effort.
[04:56] Priya: SSO integration — we use SAML with Okta. How long does SAML setup take?
[05:00] Hannah: Usually 1-2 days for a hosted pilot. Private/on-prem might take a week if there are network firewalls to open for the control plane. We'll provide an SSO runbook.
[05:11] Daniel: Network — for private we'll need a VPC peering or direct connect equivalent to your control plane. Do you support IP allowlist only?
[05:19] Carlos: We support VPC peering, VPN tunnels, and IP allowlist for certain deployments. For high-throughput private deployments we recommend peering.
[05:27] Omar: Competitors we looked at are Bedrock managed endpoints and a few specialist inference vendors — cost/SLAs vary.
[05:33] Maya: Noted.
[05:34] Priya: On audit — can we get 90 days of raw audit logs and optionally 1-year aggregated?
[05:39] Hannah: We can do configurable retention per customer; longer retention is an add-on.
[05:44] Lena: What's the usual onboarding timeline for a pilot?
[05:46] Carlos: For hosted: 1 week to onboard and run initial tests. For private on-prem: 3–6 weeks depending on procurement and infra availability. For EU-hosted private we can accelerate with our EU partner.
[06:00] Omar: Ok, sounds reasonable. Next steps?
[06:03] Maya: Recap: 1) Stonehaven to share anonymized query histograms and peak QPS. 2) Redwood to send SOC2/ISO + SSO runbook + partner MSA + pilot sizing template. 3) Set up pilot kickoff — suggest two-week window in mid-April.
[06:18] Lena: We'll aim to send histograms by EOD Friday.
[06:21] Priya: I'll review security docs and loop in audit team.
[06:25] Maya: Perfect. Anything else?
[06:27] Daniel: If you can include a rough price delta between hosted vs dedicated vs private per 1M tokens that helps procurement.
[06:34] Hannah: We'll include a ballpark cost spreadsheet.
[06:36] Maya: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
[06:42] Omar: Thanks all, bye.
